approach: Keep the round-3 design, with these changes. The replay is stored as a new typed record kind, `athena.replay/1` at `<job>/replay.json`, modelled on the existing `Baseline` record. It is not stored as `replay.md`. Adding a field to `Verification` was rejected: that struct is built literally in about nine files outside the deliverables. The records check accepts the new kind through `AnyRecord::parse` and `check_record_file`. It is written into `closing.files` as a typed record next to `brief-verifier.md`, which carries the same summary. `store.rs` needs one arm in `job_of`, because `Records::load` panics on a job record it cannot map to a job. The replay still runs `athena check-reading` from a base build and a candidate build (`BinaryDecide`) over the newest 50 accepted readings. The hold moves into `verify.rs` as a pure `hold_for_replay(&mut Judgment, list)`, since `verify.rs` is now a deliverable. The pipeline override is a `#[cfg(test)]` map keyed by repository directory. It is read first in `replay_for_job`, in front of tree resolution, the subcommand probe and the build. It returns a pair of deciders. There is no skip switch. The no-model-call criterion compares the committed invocation lists of a run with a candidate rule change and a run without one, and also checks them against a fixed expected list. History is read with `Records::load(&self.git, &head)` as run/mod.rs does, so no open question remains on that.

decisions.choice: Record the replay as a new typed record kind `athena.replay/1` (`AnyRecord::Replay(Box<Replay>)`, path `<job>/replay.json`) with `Replay { job, base_commit, candidate_commit, replayed: u32, newly_refused: Vec<ReplayRefusal{job, reason}>, held: bool, intended_percent: Option<u32>, no_replay: Option<String> }`. `validate()` requires: when `no_replay` is set, `replayed` is 0, the list is empty and `held` is false; `newly_refused.len() <= replayed`; `held` needs a non-empty list. It is pushed to `closing.files` with `NewFile::record`, as the baseline record is. No `replay.md` is created.
decisions.reason: This is the typed record the user chose, and it is accepted by the records check. I read `check_record_file`: a `.md` in a job directory other than the three in `JOB_MARKDOWN` is `UnknownFile`, which is why the first attempt failed; a `.json` at the canonical path of a parsed record is accepted. `Baseline` is the model to copy (`BASELINE_SCHEMA`, `validate`, `canonical_path`, `schema`, round-trip and misplaced tests).

rejected.why: `Verification` is built as a struct literal in land.rs, status.rs, evidence_labels.rs, introspect.rs, pr_check.rs, athena-gate/landing_tests.rs, cli/tests/reconcile.rs, run/mod.rs and reading.rs. That is about eight files outside the deliverables for one field, and it conflicts with the 'small' default.
The user chose a typed record, and a free-form file is out of scope.

rejected.option: Carry the list only in the verifier brief and the Blocker finding
rejected.why: Criteria 4, 5 and 6 need a typed record that the records check accepts and a schema round-trip.

decisions.choice: Touch `crates/athena-core/src/store.rs` for exactly one line: `AnyRecord::Replay(r) => Some(&r.job)` in `job_of`. `JobRecords` gets no new field, because its `add` already ignores unknown kinds with an `other =>` arm. Past replays are never read back.
decisions.reason: I read store.rs:324-331: any record that is not in the named arms goes to `job_of(..).expect("every other record names its job")`, so a replay record without this arm would panic `Records::load` for every later command. This is the one file outside the brief's list; it is not a governance file.

rejected.why: `JobRecords` is built literally in status.rs, steward.rs and reading.rs tests, so this would break files that are not deliverables, and nothing reads it.
`Records::load` would panic on any job directory that holds `replay.json`.

decisions.choice: The `#[cfg(test)]` override lives in run/mod.rs as `static REPLAY_OVERRIDE: Mutex<BTreeMap<PathBuf, (Arc<dyn Decide>, Arc<dyn Decide>)>>`, keyed by `self.git.dir()` (`athena-git/src/lib.rs:188`). `replay_for_job` reads it as its first statement after the empty-history check, so it sits in front of `resolve_tree`, `probe_subcommand` and the cargo build. When an entry exists, it goes straight to `replay(&cases, &*base, &*cand, &criteria)`. `Decide` is `Send + Sync`.
decisions.reason: The `repo()` fixture is not the Athena workspace, so `resolve_tree` would skip with 'no replay' and the hold test would land instead of being Rejected. Keying by the tempdir path is safe when tests run in parallel and does not depend on the thread that runs the verification.

rejected.option: Override only the cargo build step
rejected.why: Resolution and the probe would still skip in the fixture repository.

rejected.option: Seed `crates/athena-cli/Cargo.toml` and a stub binary in the fixture
rejected.why: This puts a build and a binary into every pipeline test and still tests nothing of the comparison.
It would be silently lost if verification ever ran on another thread.

decisions.choice: Compare model calls through the invocations committed for the job. Run the same fixture job in two repositories. The first has an override pair where the candidate refuses 3 of 12 seeded readings, so the job is Rejected. The second has an identical pair, so the job lands. Both must commit exactly `[(1,Reader),(2,Producer),(3,Verifier)]`, a fixed list like the one in the existing order test. No skip mode is added.
decisions.reason: Every model call goes through `invoke_and_record`, so the committed invocations are the call count. A replay that called a model would add an invocation to one run and break both the equality and the fixed list.

rejected.option: Compare with a run where the replay is skipped
rejected.why: There is no skip switch, and adding one is out of scope.

rejected.option: Read the fake driver's request list
rejected.why: The `athena()` helper hands the driver to `Athena` as `Arc<dyn AgentDriver>`, so the test has no handle to read it from.

decisions.choice: Add `pub fn hold_for_replay(judgment: &mut Judgment, list: &str)` to verify.rs. On a Pass it sets `final_verdict` to Fail, appends a `Severity::Blocker`, `FindingSource::Athena` finding naming the list, and pushes a reason. Any other verdict is left alone. run/mod.rs calls it after `judge` when the replay report is held. This is mechanism, not prose.
decisions.reason: verify.rs is now a deliverable, and `verified()` returns None unless the verdict is Pass, so the Fail blocks landing and the state becomes Rejected (run/mod.rs:2404-2409). It is pure, so it can be unit-tested.

rejected.why: It changes every `VerdictInputs` literal in the tests for no gain.

rejected.option: Hold when no replay can run
rejected.why: It would block this change's own landing, since the base has no `check-reading`, and every repository with no history.

decisions.choice: Skipped replays are recorded too. When the replay stage ran at all (including 'checks failed', 'nested run', empty history, build or probe failure), a `replay.json` with `no_replay: Some(reason)` is written, and `ReplaySummary` carries the same `no replay: <reason>` into the verifier brief, which is always written. No UI line is added for a replay that is not held.
decisions.reason: This records skips with the same typed record and brief, and answers the earlier question of how a skipped replay is recorded. The existing order test asserts exactly 6 UI lines (`said.len() == 6`), so a new line for the usual case would break it.

rejected.option: Add a UI line for every replay
rejected.why: It breaks the existing 6-line assertion at run/mod.rs:3613.

decisions.choice: Keep the earlier decisions the critic did not fault. The replay runs `athena check-reading` from a base build and a candidate build. `Decision`/`decide_stored` wrap `check_reading_acceptance(reading, request, None, &[])`. Threshold is `newly_refused * 100 > limit * replayed` with `HOLD_PERCENT = 10` as a code constant. A criterion with a percent above 10, 'refus' and an intent word replaces the limit. History is the newest 50 request jobs by id excluding the current job, with an accepted reading and a stored request. `BinaryDecide` counts only `accept` with exit 0 or `refuse: ...` with exit 1 and treats anything else as 'no replay: <reason>'. The replay runs when `nested.is_none()` and no check failed unless pre-existing. The brief section is bounded by `REPLAY_LIST_MAX` and `REPLAY_SECTION_MAX_BYTES` (6 KiB). The candidate build reuses the checks' `SnapExec` environment, and the base gets its own `SnapshotRepo::None` tree.
decisions.reason: Round 3's critique faulted none of these.

rejected.why: Both sides would carry the host's rules, so a candidate change would never show.

rejected.why: It would let loose wording switch the protection off.

risks.risk: Adding an `AnyRecord` variant breaks exhaustive matches elsewhere or panics on load.
risks.mitigation: I grepped for matches on `AnyRecord`. The only non-wildcard consumers are `parse`, `canonical_path` and `schema` in records.rs, which this change updates, and `Records::load`/`job_of` in store.rs, which gets the one arm. `JobRecords::add` and `job_of` otherwise have wildcard arms. The pipeline test loads records after a run, and `cargo test --locked` covers the rest.

risks.risk: The replay builds add minutes and disk, and a hung build stalls verification.
risks.mitigation: The candidate reuses the checks' build and environment. The base build has its own target directory, is bounded by `budget.check_timeout_s`, and is removed afterwards. Any build or probe failure becomes `no replay: <reason>` and never fails the job.

risks.risk: Existing tests and lifecycle fixtures with history would run a real build.
risks.mitigation: `replay_for_job` checks for empty history first. `resolve_tree` then skips any tree without `crates/athena-cli/Cargo.toml` with a recorded reason, so fixture repositories never reach a cargo build. The existing order test (empty history) is unchanged because no UI line is added for a non-held replay.

risks.risk: A mismatch between the host's `Reading` serialisation and a candidate that changes the struct reads as a refusal and holds a good candidate.
risks.mitigation: Only an explicit `refuse:` line with exit 1 counts. Any other exit or output makes the whole replay `no replay: <reason>`.

risks.risk: A broken replay always falls back to NoReplay and never holds, hiding the fault.
risks.mitigation: Stub-executable tests for `BinaryDecide` assert real Accept and Refuse results, and the reason is stored in the typed record and shown to the verifier.

risks.risk: The intended-rate exception matches loosely and switches the hold off.
risks.mitigation: It needs a percent above 10, 'refus' and an intent word in one criterion, and uses the stated percent as the limit. A near-miss table test covers it, and the replay is recorded either way.

risks.risk: The `#[cfg(test)]` override map leaks into production or across tests.
risks.mitigation: It is `#[cfg(test)]` only and keyed by the unique tempdir path of the repository, so parallel tests do not see each other's entries.

risks.risk: The new `replay` field breaks existing `VerifierInputs` literals or the byte-identical brief test.
risks.mitigation: `None` renders nothing, the existing byte-identical test stays as a guard, and every constructor gets `replay: None`. The section is outside the always-loaded sets, so the budget test is unaffected.

risks.risk: The hold turns a Pass into Rejected after the verifier's cost is spent.
risks.mitigation: Accepted, since the verifier must be shown the replay. The finding and the `replay.json` record the full list for a retry.

demonstrations.method: Test `replay_tests::a_stricter_candidate_rule_lists_what_it_newly_refuses` in reading.rs calls production `replay(&cases, &base, &candidate, &criteria)` over 6 fixture `ReplayCase`s (request text plus `Reading`, built like `scoped_reading`). Seam: the `Decide` trait, added in step 5, which decides accept or refuse for one case. Base is an in-process `Decide` calling the real `decide_stored`. Candidate calls `decide_stored` and also refuses requests containing a chosen common word, so it behaves like a stricter rule. One fixture is refused by both sides. demonstrations.method: Two tests on production `replay_cases(&records, &current_job)` with an in-memory `Records` (public `jobs: BTreeMap<String, JobRecords>`; `Records` is `Default` today). (a) `history_uses_newest_fifty`: 60 jobs with ascending ids and accepted readings (`job.accepted_reading` naming a stored reading, plus a stored request), plus 3 jobs with no accepted reading, 1 job whose reading exists but request is missing, and the current job. (b) `history_empty_is_no_replay`: `Records::default()` gives no cases, and `replay` on that gives `ReplayReport::NoReplay`. Seam: none; `replay_cases` and `ReplayReport` are added in step 5.
demonstrations.observes: Exactly 50 ids, newest first, which are the newest 50 jobs that have an accepted reading and a request; unaccepted, request-less and current jobs are absent. For empty history the result is the `NoReplay` variant whose `summary()` contains 'no replay', `held()` is false and `is_pass()` is false.

demonstrations.method: Table test `replay_tests::hold` on production `replay`, `ReplayReport::held`, `summary` and `intended_rate`, with fixed decider pairs over 50 cases. Seam: the `Decide` trait from step 5; the doubles only fix accept/refuse per id. Cases: 6 newly refused (12%) is held and lists 6; 5 (exactly 10%) is not held; 0 is not held; 20 (40%) with criteria 'the rule is intended to refuse about 30% of requests' is held; 12 (24%) with the same criteria is not held yet the report still lists all 12, `summary()` names the list, and the `Replay` record built from it holds `replayed` and all 12 refusals; 1 of 4 (25%) is held. A near-miss table for `intended_rate` (no percent, a percent at or below 10, a percent without 'refus', an intent word without a percent) gives no exception.
demonstrations.observes: `held()` per case as above, the list contents, and a non-empty recorded summary and record for the intended-rate case.
demonstrations.fails_without: A `>=` threshold holds the exactly-10% case. A missing criteria check holds the intended-rate case. Skipped recording leaves the intended-rate case's summary empty.

demonstrations.method: Pipeline test in `produce_and_verify_order_tests` in run/mod.rs, built on the existing `athena(&repo,&state)` and `repo()` helpers and the fake `Script`. Entry point: `Athena::go(job, AcceptedBy::User, &ui)` after `athena.ask(...)`, with `nested` None and the `probe` check passing, so the replay stage runs. Preconditions: the test first commits 12 past request jobs with a request, an accepted reading and a job record (built with `AnyRecord::to_json` and `commit_file`, like the existing tests; step 10). Seam: the `#[cfg(test)]` `REPLAY_OVERRIDE` map (step 9, new), keyed by `athena.git.dir()`, installed before `go`; it sits in front of tree resolution, the subcommand probe and the build, and returns a base decider that accepts all and a candidate decider that refuses 3 of the 12. demonstrations.observes: `finished.state` is Rejected, with no landed commit. The committed `verification.json` has a `Severity::Blocker`, `FindingSource::Athena` finding whose text names the 3 job ids. `<job>/replay.json` parses through `check_record_file` as `AnyRecord::Replay` with `replayed` 12, 3 refusals and `held` true. `Records::load(&athena.git, &head)` has an empty `invalid` list, which means the records check accepts the job directory. `git show` of `<job>/replay.md` finds nothing.
